newsitem.title: USA: Senate Republicans to announce tentative budget deal.
newsitem.headline: Senate Republicans to announce tentative budget deal.

text.p: U.S.Senate Republican leaders will announce a tentative budget and tax cut deal with the White House imminently, a Senate Republican aide said on Monday.
Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott and Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici have called a news conference to make the announcement, their press secretaries told reporters.
Domenici's spokesman, Bob Stevenson, told reporters there was "white smoke," in reference to signals used by the Vatican to announce the election of a new pope.

Republican leaders and top administration officials have been closeted in Lott's office for most of the day working out a final deal on a plan to balance the budget by 2002 and cut taxes by at least $85 billion over five years. Congressional sources have said this net tax cut could rise over $90 billion once the final numbers are calculated.

President Bill Clinton, in Las Vegas to speak to the nation's governors, had said earlier on Monday that the two sides were on the verge of an agreement and Republican leaders were equally optimistic that it could be finalised on Monday.
